title: Planning for 2027: Toll Changes That Could Affect Your Fleet
summary: Upcoming 2027 toll changes could affect fleet operating costs nationwide. See scheduled rate increases, new toll routes, and key budget considerations.
body_markdown:
[Verra Mobility Wins 2026 GovTech Breakthrough Award for Innovation in Government Technology November 11, 2026](https://www.verramobility.com/verra-mobility-wins-2026-govtech-award/)


As fleets prepare for 2027, toll expenses deserve a closer look. Approved rate increases, changes to payment discounts and expanding toll networks will affect operating costs across several major U.S. markets.


For organizations managing hundreds or thousands of vehicles, even modest adjustments can add up. Understanding where changes are scheduled and how they apply to different vehicles and payment methods can help fleet managers build more accurate budgets.


## Northeast: Higher Rates and Changing Discounts


The


[Pennsylvania Turnpike](https://www.paturnpike.com/media-center/pa-turnpike-blog/details/blog/2026/07/08/understanding-the-pa-turnpikes-2027-toll-rates) will implement a 3.5% toll increase effective January 3, 2027. Although this is its smallest percentage increase since 2014, fleets traveling regularly across the system should incorporate the adjustment into route budgets.


The


[New York State Thruway](https://thruway.ny.gov/about/thruway-toll-adjustment) will implement its next approved systemwide adjustment on January 1, 2027, including a 5% increase to base New York E-ZPass rates. The Governor Mario M. Cuomo Bridge will also receive its scheduled $0.50 increase to base New York E-ZPass tolls.


At


[Port Authority of New York and New Jersey crossings](https://www.panynj.gov/content/dam/corporate/public-hearings-pdfs/Approved_Fee_Changes_Toll_and_Bus.pdf) , the E-ZPass off-peak discount for eligible passenger vehicles and motorcycles will decrease from $2 to $1.50 on January 3, 2027. This begins a four-year phaseout and is separate from other scheduled toll adjustments.


In


[New Hampshire](https://gc.nh.gov/rsa/html/XX/237/237-mrg.htm) , new schedules effective January 1, 2027 increase tolls for cash transactions and vehicles not listed on a funded New Hampshire E-ZPass account. For example, the new Class 1 rate at Hooksett Main will be $2 for these transactions. The distinction depends on the toll account, not simply the vehicle’s registration state.


## Midwest: Significant Increases and More Frequent Adjustments


The


[Illinois Tollway](https://agency.illinoistollway.com/drivingconnections#TollRateIncrease) has approved a 30% increase in commercial vehicle toll rates beginning January 1, 2027. Passenger vehicle tolls will rise by approximately $0.45 per toll. Businesses operating mixed fleets should review vehicle classifications before applying a single budget assumption across all vehicles.


The


[Ohio Turnpike](https://www.ohioturnpike.org/schedule-of-tolls-%282024-2028%29) will increase toll rates by 2.7% on January 1, 2027, under its approved multiyear schedule.


The


[Indiana Toll Road](https://indianacapitalchronicle.com/2026/04/15/indiana-toll-road-deal-would-trade-twice-annual-hikes-for-700m-bears-stadium-windfall/) is moving to a framework permitting toll adjustments twice a year, beginning December 31, 2026, with subsequent adjustment dates on June 30 and December 31 each year.


The RiverLink crossings connecting


[Louisville and Southern Indiana](https://riverlink.com/tolling-options-rates/) also warrant a midyear budget review. Existing policy calls for tolls to increase each July 1 by 2.5% or the applicable inflation rate, whichever is higher.


## South Central: Changes in Oklahoma and Texas


The


[Oklahoma Turnpike Authority](https://oklahoma.gov/ota/media/newsroom/2026/november/ota-board-adopts-scheduled-toll-adjustment--kicks-off-second-yea.html) has approved new rates effective January 5, 2027, designed to increase systemwide toll revenue by 6%. Individual trip increases will vary.


In Texas, the


[City of Laredo International Bridge System](https://www.cityoflaredo.com/departments/bridge-system) will begin a phased adjustment on January 1, 2027, increasing southbound commercial and noncommercial vehicle tolls by $0.50 per axle. Businesses with cross-border operations should incorporate the change into trip estimates.


## California:


Bay Area Bridge Toll Changes Ahead in 2027


On January 1, 2027, seven state-owned


[Bay Area bridges](https://www.bayareafastrak.com/en/cms/news-detail-article34.shtml) will introduce payment-based pricing alongside their scheduled increase: Antioch, Benicia-Martinez, Carquinez, Dumbarton, Richmond-San Rafael, San Mateo-Hayward and San Francisco–Oakland Bay.


The


[Golden Gate Bridge](https://www.goldengate.org/golden-gate-bridge-district-approves-new-five-year-toll-program/) follows a separate schedule. Its approved five-year toll program includes another $0.50 increase for two-axle vehicles on July 1, 2027, making both January and midyear adjustments relevant to Bay Area fleet budgets.


## North Carolina: New Tolls on Vehicle Ferry Routes


New toll exposure is not limited to roads and bridges.


The


[No rth Carolina Department of Transportation](https://www.ncdot.gov/divisions/ferry/Pages/ferry-tolls.aspx) will begin collecting tolls on four previously


untolled


vehicle ferry routes on January 1, 2027.


Service and delivery fleets


operating


in coastal communities should review vehicle sizing and payment requirements before applying these base rates across their operations.


## New Tolled Routes Could Change Fleet Travel


Several projects are expected to expand tolled travel options in 2027:


- **Pennsylvania:** The


[PA Turnpike is converting to Open Road Tolling (ORT](https://www.paturnpike.com/all-electronic-tolling/open-road-tolling)


). The system will go live statewide on January 3, 2027, completing the western and central transition.


- **Washington:** The


[I-405 Renton to Bellevue express toll lane expansion](https://wsdot.wa.gov/construction-planning/search-projects/i-405renton-bellevue-widening-and-express-toll-lanes-project) is expected to open in summer 2027, adding another option for fleets serving the Seattle area.


- **Illinois:** The


[I-490/Illinois Route 390 interchange](https://agency.illinoistollway.com/projects/490/interchange)


is scheduled for completion by the end of 2027, adding roadway and connections serving the west side of O’Hare International Airport.


- **Virginia:** VDOT anticipates completion of the


[Hampton Roads Express Lanes’](https://www.vdot.virginia.gov/projects/major-projects/64expresslanes/)


Newport News segment in spring 2027 and Hampton segment in summer 2027.


- **Maryland:** The


[I-95 Express Toll Lanes northbound extension](https://mdta.maryland.gov/I95ETLNB/home.html) to north of MD 24 is expected to open by the end of 2027.


## Additional Changes to Monitor


Not every agency has finalized its 2027 rates. Fleets should continue checking updates from the


[New Jersey Turnpike Authority](https://www.njta.gov/) ,


[Central Florida Expressway Authority](https://www.cfxway.com/for-travelers/tolls/toll-rates/) ,


[Tampa Hillsborough Expressway Authority](https://tampa-xway.com/for-travelers/tolls/toll-map-calculator/) and


[North Texas Tollway Authority](https://www.ntta.org/) .


MTA financial materials also identify a


[proposed March 2027 fare and toll adjustment](https://www.mta.info/document/180861) , which should be monitored for finalized toll schedules.


As toll rates and networks evolve, centralized management can help fleets maintain visibility and reduce administrative work.
